To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ER status is concordant in the majority of primary breast carcinomas (79%) and their lymph node (LN) metastases.

(1) ERs were lost in 21% of the lymph node metastases compared to their primary tumours, and (2) the ID5 monoclonal antibody performed better than the ER‐ICA monoclonal antibody in the immunohistochemical analysis of ERs on paraffin‐fixed breast cancer tissues.
(1) The ER status in the primary tumour and the lymph node metastases was concordant or discordant in 79% or 21% of cases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ER status in primary breast carcinoma and their metastases.
the study of ERs in primary and secondary breast tumours and the evaluation of two different monoclonal antibodies for the determination of ER status in breast carcinomas.
the study of ER status in breast cancer and its prognostic and/or therapeutic implications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the paraffin ERICA test on paraffin‐fixed tissue is an excellent screening test for ER‐positive breast cancer, but that it should not be used to determine the ER status of a tumour when the result of this test will be used as the basis for therapeutic decisions.
ID5 antibody on paraffined tissue has the same sensitivity and specificity as ER‐ICA antibody in the detection of ERs in breast cancer.
the ID5 antibody is a reliable and sensitive marker for ERs in paraffin‐processed material, although the sensitivity is lower than that of the ER‐ICA antibody.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
paraffin ER immunohistochemistry is reliable for the determination of ER status of primary carcinomas but not of their lymph node metastasis.
the ID5 antibody is a reliable method for detection of ERs in paraffin‐fixed tissue, and that it is a useful tool for retrospective studies.
paraffin‐ER‐ICA was as good as frozen‐ER‐ICA, but that ID5 was better than ER‐ICA on paraffin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ID5 antibody on paraffined tissue is an excellent alternative to frozen tissue ER‐ICA for routine diagnostic ER analyses.
immunohistochemistry of ER on paraffin‐fixed tissue is a reliable method for the determination of ER status.

the ID5 antibody on formalin‐ fixed paraffin‐ embedded tissue is an accurate and practical method for ER‐status analysis in breast carcinoma, and may be a good substitute for the ER‐ICA assay on fresh tissue.
